notes.title: Demo Update - v.0.3.64
notes.content:
To prepare for Steam Next Fest in June 2025, a major update has been released for the demo version:

[list]
[*] Added [b]Arcade Mode[/b], unlocked after a successful demo playthrough
[*] Added [b]Library[/b] with gameplay tips
[*] Added [b]Training Room[/b] to try out skills
[*] Added [b]Gear Room[/b] for equipping different skins
[*] Each mission now consists of 6 floors (previously 4)
[*] Floors now feature more enemies and increased difficulty
[*] XP Coins are now "sucked in" (Sekiro-style)
[*] Throwing balls with a gamepad stops the player for better aiming
[*] Throwing balls with a mouse does not stop the player (because why not)
[*] Improved Savegame loading display
[/list]

notes.title: C.T.E. Awareness Day 2025
notes.content:
Tackle for Loss is brutal, fast, and hopefully fun—but beneath that lies a harsh reality. The main character, a football player in the ‘80s, doesn’t know what’s happening to him. But today, we do. His struggles mirror those of real-life athletes affected by CTE (Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy), a condition that was unknown at the time but is all too real now.

CTE Awareness Day just passed, but it’s never too late to pause and reflect. If you’ve never heard of CTE, take a few minutes to learn more: [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chronic_traumatic_encephalopathy]CTE Wikipedia[/url]. My own deep dive into this topic started with [url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/315762/the-ghost-in-my-brain-by-clark-elliott-phd/]The Ghost in My Brain[/url] by Clark Elliott—a book I highly recommend.

Take care of your mind, your body, and each other. Stay healthy. 🏈❤️
Daniel

notes.title: Announcement Reveal Trailer Is Here!
notes.content:
Behold Werner Herzog-style gravitas from a German developer! Tackle for Loss is not all about fun and games, but also aims at nothing less than improving the world beyond gaming by raising awareness to the dangers of concussions and their disastrous consequences.

[h3]Today I proudly present the reveal trailer for Tackle for Loss.[/h3]

I felt the need to distill in this trailer what makes this game special: besides the obvious key features (you tackle and juke like an American football pro to eliminate your opponents) it's the dark and scary consequences of brain damage that can result from concussions. 

Enough of words, now go and watch the teaser:

notes.title: Open Beta is coming!
notes.content:
[b]BERLIN, GERMANY, August 8, 2024[/b] - Indifferent Penguin, a Berlin-based solo game developer, is calling for dedicated gamers to join the open beta of its upcoming top-down action game, Tackle for Loss. In this game, players delve into the gritty underbelly of 1980s American Football. Inspired by the likes of Hotline Miami, Tackle for Loss blends violent combat, a captivating narrative, and dark pixel art aesthetics.

[h4]About the beta:[/h4]
A Windows PC and Gamepad are required. Participants will receive a free Steam key. Slots are limited. To join, follow this link: [url=https://mailchi.mp/44b9f1f0e5ba/tackleforloss]https://mailchi.mp/44b9f1f0e5ba/tackleforloss[/url] (Deadline for application: August 31, 2024)

[h4]About the game:[/h4]
Tackle for Loss is a 2D top-down action game that puts you in the shoes of a former American football pro. Violent combat, a captivating narrative, and dark pixel art combine to create a pumped-up experience, inspired by the likes of Hotline Miami. The player is haunted by the lingering effects of concussions and driven by a desperate mission to save a loved one. Utilizing his unique set of football skills, players will navigate a gritty underworld, battling enemies and unraveling a conspiracy in the process.

Rapidly eliminating enemies extends combo chains and increases score multipliers, rewarding players for aggressive and strategic gameplay. Unique moves and attacks can be unlocked through progression. By experimenting with a variety of skills and perks, players can develop and refine a variety of combat styles.

In its core, Tackle for Loss is a game about the brutal beauty of football, but it also inadvertently shines a spotlight on the darker side of the sport. By immersing players in the life of a former player struggling with the long-term consequences of his career, the game offers a glimpse into the realities of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE).

"I wanted to create a game that captured the raw energy and violence of American football, but from a completely different angle," said Daniel Wichterich, the developer behind Indifferent Penguin. "Tackle for Loss is my attempt to explore the darker side of the sport, while still delivering the adrenaline-pumping action that gamers crave."

"While the football simulation genre is dominated by massive titles, I believe there’s a gap in the market for a game that takes the core elements of the sport and reimagines them in a fresh and exciting way," Wichterich continued. "Tackle for Loss aims to fill that void."

Tackle for Loss is currently in development, targeting a late 2025 release on Windows PC. The game has received funding from the Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg, a German film and media funding agency. The game is available to wishlist on Steam now.

Download Presskit (~50mb):
[url=https://indifferentpenguin.de/files/TackleForLossPressKit.zip]https://indifferentpenguin.de/files/TackleForLossPressKit.zip[/url]

[h4]About Indifferent Penguin[/h4]
Indifferent Penguin is a solo game development studio based in Berlin, Germany. Founded by Daniel Wichterich in 2023, the studio is passionate about creating unique and engaging gaming experiences that push the boundaries of traditional genres.

Website:
[url=https://indifferentpenguin.de]https://indifferentpenguin.de[/url]
